facts.statement: Mullerornis modestus is the sole species within the extinct genus Mullerornis.
facts.quote: Mullerornis modestus is an extinct species of elephant bird, and the only member of the genus Mullerornis.

facts.statement: The genus Mullerornis was formally described in 1894 by Alphonse Milne-Edwards and Alfred Grandidier.
facts.quote: The genus Mullerornis was described in 1894 by Alphonse Milne-Edwards & Alfred Grandidier.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Georges Muller, a French explorer killed in 1892 by the Sakalava people.
facts.quote: The genus is named after Georges Muller, a French explorer, who was killed in 1892 by hostile members of the Sakalava people.

facts.statement: Mullerornis was smaller than Aepyornis, reaching a height of 1.49 meters and weighing approximately 80 kg.
facts.quote: Mullerornis is smaller than the more well-known Aepyornis, with a still substantial body mass of approximately 80 kg, along with a height of 1.49 meters (4.88 ft).

facts.statement: Radiocarbon dating of a bone suggests Mullerornis survived until approximately 1260 years before present.
facts.quote: A bone possibly belonging to Mullerornis has been radiocarbon dated to about 1260 BP, suggesting that the animal was still extant at the end of the first millennium.

facts.statement: Based on optic lobe size, Mullerornis was likely nocturnal but may have also been active during twilight.
facts.quote: Like other elephant birds and its kiwi relatives, Mullerornis probably was nocturnal based on the small size of its optic lobes, though it shows less optical lobe reduction than these other taxa, implying slightly more crepuscular habits.

facts.statement: Isotopic evidence indicates that Mullerornis was a browsing herbivore.
facts.quote: Isotopic evidence suggests that Mullerornis was likely a browsing herbivore.

facts.statement: Mullerornis eggs were much smaller than those of Aepyornis, weighing about 0.86 kg with a shell thickness of 1.1 mm.
facts.quote: The eggs of Mullerornis are substantially smaller than those of Aepyornis, weighting approximately 0.86 kg, with a shell thickness of about 1.1 mm.

facts.statement: Mullerornis was an extinct elephant bird from Madagascar that went extinct approximately one millennium ago.
facts.quote: Mullerornis es un género extinto de aves Struthioniformes de la familia Aepyornithidae, conocidos como las aves elefante que vivieron en Madagascar, que se extingieron hace aproximadamente un milenio, ya que se ha encontrado un hueso, posiblemente de un Mullerornis, fechado por radiocarbono en el 1260.

facts.statement: Mullerornis is classified in the order Struthioniformes and the family Aepyornithidae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Aves ordo: Struthioniformes familia: †Aepyornithidae genus: †Mullerornis

facts.statement: Mullerornis lived during the Late Pleistocene to Holocene, from 0.129 to 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)
